clue.text: It's a sort of bird, we affirm

parts.note: taken as written
to aver is to affirm or declare

explanation.surface: Two people solemnly declare that something is a kind of bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The weaver is a family of finches famous for knotting elaborate grass nests.

clue.text: I'm happier somehow, having abandoned pious biblical tribe

indicators.note: somehow says the letters of the words before it are rearranged in some fashion

parts.note: pi is a common slang abbreviation for pious

explanation.surface: Someone feels more cheerful after giving up a religious tribe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having abandoned' tells you PI must come out: the letters of I'M HAPPIER are the answer's plus PI, and the indicator word signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephraim was one of the twelve tribes of Israel, named after a son of Joseph.

clue.text: Appreciate having very small drink outside university

indicators.note: outside says the drink wraps around the next piece

parts.note: small beer is weak ale, so a small drink is ale

explanation.surface: Enjoying a modest drink just off campus.
explanation.definitionFit: To appreciate something is to value it, both verbs of esteem.

clue.text: Glow of fantastic sunrise seen across two days

indicators.note: seen across means the scrambled word spans the other piece, enclosing it
fantastic suggests the letters are wildly reworked

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for day, so two days are DD

explanation.surface: A sunrise glows so splendidly that it seems to last two days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fantastic' makes RUINESS from SUNRISE, and 'seen across' puts DD inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruddiness is a healthy red colour or flush, the same as a glow in the cheeks.

clue.text: A community that's prosperous but not quiet?

definitions.text: A community that's prosperous but not quiet?

parts.words: A community that's prosperous but not quiet?
parts.note: a thriving settlement, but read literally as a noisy place, since a boom is a loud bang

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a wealthy community must also be a noisy one.
explanation.definitionFit: A town enjoying sudden economic growth is said to boom, while boom is also a loud noise.

clue.text: Blade makes opening initially in reddish-brown material

indicators.note: in places the first letter inside the run of the other two pieces

parts.note: bay is a reddish-brown colour, used of horses
net is a mesh fabric

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A knife is made by cutting into reddish-brown cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A bayonet is a blade fixed to the muzzle of a rifle.

clue.text: Part of New Zealand's collection of books in the past

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a collection of books of the Bible
ago means in the past

explanation.surface: A region of New Zealand once held a library.
explanation.definitionFit: Otago is a region in the south of New Zealand's South Island.

clue.text: Time to study philosopher? It's routine drudgery

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it at university
John Stuart Mill was a British philosopher

explanation.surface: Is it time to study a philosopher, or is that just drudgery?
explanation.definitionFit: A treadmill figuratively means a tedious repetitive round of work.

clue.text: Spiteful desire to squash snake

indicators.note: to squash in means the desire is pressed around the snake

parts.note: a wish is a desire
the asp is a small venomous snake

explanation.surface: A spiteful wish to crush a snake underfoot.
explanation.definitionFit: Waspish means irritable and sharply spiteful, like a stinging insect.

clue.text: Yokelish drama excited visitors to the seaside pier?

indicators.note: excited suggests the letters are stirred up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Country-bumpkin theatre performed on a pier thrills the seaside crowds.
explanation.definitionFit: Tourists on a seaside break are typical holiday visitors who stroll on piers.

clue.text: Hurried to far end of valley to grab one plant

indicators.note: to the far end of tells you the hurrying piece is attached after the valley

parts.note: a vale is a valley

indicators.note: to grab means the hurrying word takes hold of the numeral inside it

parts.note: ran means hurried
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone rushes to the far end of a valley to pick a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Valerian is a flowering plant whose root is used as a herbal sedative.

clue.text: Decree from old duke stuck in wet weather

indicators.note: stuck in says one piece is lodged inside the other

parts.note: rain is wet weather

explanation.surface: An elderly duke caught in the rain issues an order.
explanation.definitionFit: To ordain is to decree or order officially.

clue.text: Smear from self-satisfied English about Germany

indicators.note: about means the first pieces go around the next one

parts.note: smug means self-satisfied
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: A smug Englishman's slur against the Germans.
explanation.definitionFit: A smudge is a smear or blurred mark.

clue.text: Copy political party with untruth about woman being nasty?

parts.note: the DUP is the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland

indicators.note: about means the untruth surrounds the next piece

parts.note: a lie is an untruth
a cat is a spiteful woman

explanation.surface: Politicians copy a lie about a woman behaving badly.
explanation.definitionFit: A duplicate is an exact copy.

clue.text: Obscure group of women beginning to laugh coming in drunk

indicators.note: coming in says the women and first letter enter the drunk word

parts.note: tight is slang for drunk
WI is the Women's Institute, a British community organisation for women

indicators.note: beginning to picks the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Shadowy group of women starts laughing as they stagger in tipsy.
explanation.definitionFit: Twilight is dimness or half-darkness, and obscure as a noun means darkness.

clue.text: All right for getting covered, wearing fur around old city

parts.note: in means wearing, as in dressed in

indicators.note: around means the fur wraps the next piece

parts.note: sable is a valuable fur
Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: It is fine to cover up in fur when visiting an ancient city.
explanation.definitionFit: Insurable means suitable to be insured, i.e. acceptable for cover.

clue.text: After drink, sat and hypothesised

indicators.note: after puts the sitting word behind the drink

parts.note: to sup is to drink
posed, as for a portrait, means sat

explanation.surface: Someone had a drink, sat down and began theorising.
explanation.definitionFit: Supposed means assumed or hypothesised.

clue.text: Implement let us in after manipulation

indicators.note: after manipulation says the letters have been handled and rearranged

explanation.surface: A tool begs to be let in after it has been handled.
explanation.definitionFit: A utensil is a tool or implement, especially in the kitchen.

clue.text: Expert concealing old company's shortfall

indicators.note: concealing means the expert word hides the company inside it

parts.note: deft means skilful or expert
ICI was Imperial Chemical Industries, a former British company

explanation.surface: A skilled accountant hides an old firm's losses.
explanation.definitionFit: A deficit is an amount by which something falls short.

clue.text: Single maiden with name for being poker-faced

parts.note: sole means single or only
M is the cricket abbreviation for maiden over

explanation.surface: An unmarried young woman keeps a straight face.
explanation.definitionFit: Solemn means grave and serious, without showing emotion.

clue.text: Maiden has upset cat? A blunder

parts.note: a miss is an unmarried young woman

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the animal word is turned over, read upwards

parts.note: a cat kept at home is a pet

explanation.surface: A young lady upsets her cat, a clumsy mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns PET into TEP, which follows MISS.
explanation.definitionFit: A misstep is a false step, hence a mistake or blunder.

clue.text: To blame for running late

explanation.definitionFit: Behind can mean the cause of something, or lagging after the expected time.

clue.text: Lazy type finished outside front of restaurant

indicators.note: outside means the finished word wraps the next letter

parts.note: done means finished

indicators.note: front of takes the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: An idler has had enough outside a restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: A drone is a male bee that does no work, hence a lazy person.

clue.text: Lacking order by reason of getting left in muddle

parts.note: for can mean because of

indicators.note: in means left is placed inside the muddle

parts.note: a mess is a muddle

explanation.surface: Things go wrong because someone is left in a muddle.
explanation.definitionFit: Formless means without shape or structure, so lacking order.

clue.text: Weapon, something for sale put out by knight

indicators.note: put out by means the item for sale is removed from the knight

parts.note: Lancelot was a knight of King Arthur's Round Table
a lot is an item put up for sale at auction

explanation.surface: A knight discards a weapon at an auction.
explanation.definitionFit: A lance is a long spear carried by knights.

clue.text: Opposition group kept slightly in the dark?

definitions.meaning: the leading opposition politicians who mirror government ministers
read literally, a cupboard placed in the shade

explanation.definitionFit: The opposition's team of spokesmen mirrors the government cabinet and is named for being in its shade.

clue.text: Run away from ordeal most quickly

parts.note: to flee is to run away from
a test is a trial or ordeal

explanation.surface: Escaping a trial at top speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleet means swift, so the superlative is the swiftest.

clue.text: Excuse offered by old lover meaningless almost

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: empty means meaningless, as in empty words

explanation.surface: A former partner offers an excuse that means almost nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To exempt someone is to excuse them from a duty.
